title: Connection lifecycle policies: idle-pruning, proactive reconnects, and per-route timeout profiles
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: SDKs currently expose coarse transport knobs (global timeouts, a basic keepalive) but teams building long-lived streaming or bursty request patterns see two recurring issues: (1) idle TCP/TLS connections piling up and not being reclaimed, increasing file descriptor pressure and memory; (2) head-of-line latency spikes when an old connection degrades mid-stream (TLS renegotiation / NAT timeouts) because clients don't proactively rotate connections or use per-route timeout/connect profiles.

Goals: Provide a cross-SDK pattern and default configuration for connection lifecycle that: (a) safely prunes idle connections, (b) proactively rotates/refreshes connections for long-lived streaming sessions to avoid mid-stream stalls, (c) allows per-route timeout/connect profiles (short timeouts forinteractive chat, long for batch/streaming), and (d) surfaces metrics and knobs consistently across Python/TS/Go.

Non-goals: Replacing application-level retry semantics (we will integrate but not change idempotency rules), implementing custom TCP stack logic, or changing server-side behavior.

Proposed API (cross-language shape): Introduce a top-level `transport` block with optional `profiles` that can be referenced per-client or per-request. Profile keys: `connect_timeout_ms`, `request_timeout_ms`, `idle_conn_ttl_ms`, `max_idle_per_host`, `keepalive_interval_ms`, `proactive_reconnect_threshold_pct` (rotate connection after N% of TTL), `enable_stream_rotation` (bool), and `graceful_drain_ms`. Example intent: `profiles: { low_latency: {...}, streaming: {...} }` then attach via `client.withProfile('streaming')` or request option `{transportProfile: 'low_latency'}`.

Language examples (to be shipped as examples folder):
- Python (requests/asyncio + httpx adapter): show client-level `profiles` and a `with_profile` context manager that sets proactive rotation for long streaming iterators.
- TypeScript (fetch/node): provide wrapper that exposes `transport.profiles` plus a `stream.rotate()` helper consumed by server-sent events / eventsource streams.
- Go (http.Client): show `TransportProfile` struct and helper to attach profile to `http.Request` using context.

Streaming ergonomics: `enable_stream_rotation` allows the SDK to pre-emptively open a fresh connection and gracefully migrate a long-running stream within `graceful_drain_ms`. For non-upgrade streams (SSE/HTTP2) rotation will open a second connection and drain tokens; for single-connection protocols (HTTP/1.1 chunked) rotation becomes a best-effort reconnect with resume semantics documented and opt-in.

Retries and idempotency: SDK will not silently retry streaming payloads that are non-idempotent. For short non-streaming requests, the per-profile `request_timeout_ms` plus a standardized retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter) will be used when request is idempotent or when caller opts-in via header `X-Redwood-Retry-Allow`. We will include clear examples to avoid double-execution.

Metrics & telemetry: Emit `transport.profile.<name>.conn_count`, `transport.profile.<name>.idle_pruned_total`, `transport.profile.<name>.proactive_rotate_total`, `transport.profile.<name>.avg_conn_age_ms`, and histogram `transport.connect_latency_ms`. These will be wired into the Console per-route breakdowns.

Acceptance criteria: (1) consistent config API implemented in Python/TS/Go SDKs; (2) bench microtests show idle FD reduction >= 30% for typical chat workloads and median p50 latency improvement during 30m streams by >= 10% due to rotation; (3) integration tests that simulate NAT idle expiry and demonstrate graceful rotation without silent duplicate deliveries; (4) docs + 3 examples (one per language) and a migration note.

Rollout: Feature-flag rollout in hosted SDK binding (opt-in profile names visible in Console). Coordinate with runtime team for compatibility; gradual rollout across customers with canary percent and metrics review.

Deliverables: SDK PRs for each language, integration test harness (k6 + local proxy that forces connection resets), design doc in Confluence, and Console metric dashboards and alerts.

2025-02-14 - Marcus Li: Added per-route profiles API sketch. Will prototype in TypeScript first to validate ergonomics against existing fetch wrapper.
2025-02-20 - Sofia García (Design): Reviewed sample UX for JS `withProfile` and suggested `client.withProfile('name')` instead of per-request verbose options for common cases.

2025-02-24 - Marcus Li: Bench completed against chat workload (10k short-lived requests + 200 concurrent 30m streams). Observed ~38% fewer idle FDs when `idle_conn_ttl_ms`=300000 and `max_idle_per_host`=10. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123

2025-02-27 - Ethan Brooks (SRE): Confirmed metrics names and added `transport.profile.<name>.idle_pruned_total` to runtime ingestion. Suggested adding alert when `proactive_rotate_total` spikes unexpectedly.
